title: ab-ovo content bundle, schema version 1
$comment: THE CONTRACT BETWEEN N CONTENT COMPILERS AND ONE APPLICATION.
This repository owns the schema; each track owns its own compiler and its own content
repository (book issue #239 §6). The book's compiler is one producer and a Python
track's compiler will be another, so nothing in here may assume the content is a book
of frames — the minimum unit is a title and a body, and the Stroud mechanics
(question, covered answer, next-frame cue) are ONE step kind rather than the shape of
a step.
It is JSON Schema rather than a TypeScript type because the first producer is Python.
A contract the producer cannot check is a contract the producer discovers by having a
bundle rejected, and #239 §1 requires the opposite: 'The compiler REFUSES rather than
degrades.' It needs something to refuse against before it attaches a bundle to a
release.
validate.ts enforces this document by READING it rather than by restating it, so the
two cannot drift — and it refuses outright a schema using a keyword it does not
implement, because a validator that silently ignores a constraint is indistinguishable
from one that passes.
WHAT JSON SCHEMA CANNOT SAY, and validate.ts therefore also checks: that a cue is
followed by an answer and an answer is preceded by a cue; that steps are contiguous
from 1; that every range endpoint and every section anchor names a step that exists;
that every declared language is present in every text. Each of those is a defect the
book's own gates were written after shipping — a Quiz route to frames 91-93 of a
48-frame program passed every check it had.

schemaVersion.$comment: Refused rather than best-efforted when unknown. A partial render of a bundle from a newer compiler is a page that looks finished.

tag.$comment: The content tag. The application pins (track, tag) PAIRS, never a tag alone (#239 §6), and phase 4 records outcomes against a frame IN A BUNDLE VERSION so a rate never averages a reader's experience of two different texts.

languages.$comment: Every language this track claims. Every text in the bundle must carry every one of them — a half-translated bundle renders a blank where a reader expected prose.

units.$comment: Ordered. A unit is the navigable thing — a program here, a lesson elsewhere.

labs.$comment: Optional: a track may have no runnable exercises at all. Each entry is a reference, never the exercise text — the lab engine is fetched from the track's own repository and its layout is load-bearing.

text.$comment: A string per language code. Checked against track.languages by validate.ts, which JSON Schema cannot do because the key set is data.

sections.$comment: HEADINGS, NOT A LEVEL OF THE TREE. The book navigates by unit and step and never by section — 'every Summary back-reference, every Quiz route and every cross-reference in the book names a program and a frame'. Modelling sections as a container would put a level in the schema that nothing addresses.

routes.$comment: A Quiz item, an outcome, a Summary bracket: anything that sends a reader back to a span of steps. One shape for all of them, because the failure they share is an endpoint that does not exist.

step.$comment: THE MINIMUM UNIT IS title + body (#239 §6). Everything else is a property of one kind of step. A track with no frames renders from title and body alone rather than faking a question nobody asked.

answer.$comment: THE OPENING OF THIS STEP, WHICH ANSWERS THE PREVIOUS ONE. That is the book's own mechanic — '\ans{} opens a frame with the previous frame's answer' — and reproducing it rather than inventing a parallel one is what makes the answer ABSENT from the DOM before a reveal rather than merely hidden: deliver one step at a time and the next step's opening has not been sent yet.

cue.$comment: 'The next step opens with an answer.' True if and only if step n+1 carries one, which validate.ts checks in both directions — the book's C16, whose whole reason for existing is that a cue dropped from both editions at once is invisible to every check that compares them.

check.$comment: The optional check of #239 §6's minimum unit. A reference into labs[], never an exercise body.

runtime.$comment: #239 §6: the track manifest names the runtime each lab needs, so the application loads numpy only for the labs that say so and the cost is a decision rather than a default.
